harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired writer.py for Python 2.4.3. It now reopens audit.log on SIGHUP without restarting, releases the old descriptor, and closes cleanly on SIGTERM. Existing archive records were preserved. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged, and node1 passed the mandatory reboot persistence check.
actions_performed: Added Python 2.4-compatible SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers.
Verified live log rotation while retaining the same process identity.
Verified the rotated file stopped growing and only current audit.log remained open.
Verified SIGTERM exited cleanly with no remaining log holders.
Safely rebooted node1 and revalidated source, data, signal behavior, OS, and kernel.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP reopens audit.log without process restart and releases the old descriptor
evidence.summary: PID 3489 and start_ticks 22838 remained unchanged; the rotated file stayed at 656 bytes while the new audit.log grew from 48 to 80 bytes, with only the current path held open.

evidence.requirement: SIGTERM closes the log and exits cleanly
evidence.summary: The writer exited, log size remained stable, and no recovery-log descriptors remained open.
archive/previous.log retained checksum 5355b97cc10231092b2bf7bc7c31d12f66508a8d and the A100 record before and after changes and reboot.
writer.py byte-compiled under Python 2.4.3; CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained installed.

Captured healthy baseline, acknowledged native safe reboot, observed boot ID change from 271d28a6-6ec8-4c6f-8000-000000000000 to aafb66d7-923c-44ff-8000-000000000000, confirmed matching data/source checksums, and passed post-reboot SIGHUP/SIGTERM runtime verification.
